frozen_hypothesis: A pack that only qualifies inside its producing process is detectable by re-qualifying across a process boundary.
frozen_required_deliverable: A cross-process re-qualification harness that compares in-process and subprocess qualification verdicts and reports divergence.

hidden_cases.rationale: The decisive question for this unit. The frozen hypothesis is about a PACK that only qualifies inside its producing process, and unit 017's real pack qualification engine sits in the same cohort. Can this harness actually be pointed at it?
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim: HC-C real qualify_pack.py exit: 1 | error: AttributeError: module 'synthetic_qualifier' has no attribute 'prime_producer_memory'
hidden_cases.interpretation: The harness cannot be applied to any real qualifier. It requires the target to implement a bespoke two-function protocol - prime_producer_memory() and qualify() returning a dict with 'qualified' and 'fixture_label' - which nothing in the repository implements except the fixture shipped alongside it. Pointed at the cohort's own real pack qualification engine it dies with an unhandled AttributeError rather than failing closed with a structured error. So the harness's reach over real pack qualification is zero, and it does not fail safe on a non-conforming target.

synthetic_evidence_assessment.does_the_synthetic_case_stand_in_for_the: NO, and this is my central finding. The synthetic fixture proves the COMPARISON MECHANISM works - I confirmed that myself in both directions with a working negative control. But no pack is qualified anywhere in this unit. The harness operates on a Python module implementing an interface invented for this unit, not on a pack, a manifest, or a pinned commit. The frozen hypothesis is about 'a pack that only qualifies inside its producing process', and the demonstrated artifact never qualifies a pack at all. The evidence is therefore circular in the specific sense that matters: it detects process-memory dependence in a fixture whose entire purpose is to have process-memory dependence, and it cannot be aimed at anything else.
synthetic_evidence_assessment.is_this_fixable: Yes, and cheaply, which is why I judge NOT_YET rather than NOT_SUPPORTED. Unit 017's qualify_pack.qualify(repo, commit, manifest_path) is an ordinary function. Importing it and calling it in-process, then invoking qualify_pack.py as a subprocess on the same pinned pack and comparing the two verdicts, would make this unit's claim real using material already committed in the same cohort.

producer_declared_limitations: The divergence fixture is synthetic and demonstrates detection mechanics; it does not assert that every published pack has process-memory coupling.
scope_honesty_assessment.assessment: The producer is admirably candid that the fixture is synthetic and demonstrates 'detection mechanics'. That phrasing is honest and it is close to my own conclusion. But the limitation as written disclaims the wrong thing. It disclaims a claim nobody would make - that every published pack has this coupling - while leaving unstated the material fact that the harness cannot be applied to ANY real pack qualifier, including the cohort's own unit-017 engine, and crashes with an unhandled AttributeError when tried. The producer also did not supply the negative control, without which even the mechanics claim was unproven; I had to establish it.

reproducibility_check: All three hidden cases and the producer test were run in fresh python3 -I processes and reproduced identically. The harness sets sys.dont_write_bytecode before loading the fixture, so no bytecode is emitted.
divergence_reason: The frozen hypothesis concerns 'a pack that only qualifies inside its producing process', and no pack is qualified anywhere in this unit. The harness only accepts targets implementing a bespoke prime_producer_memory()/qualify() protocol that nothing in the repository implements except the fixture shipped beside it. When I pointed it at the cohort's own real pack qualification engine (unit 017's qualify_pack.py) it died with an unhandled AttributeError rather than failing closed. The comparison mechanism itself is sound - I verified it detects divergence in both directions and correctly returns PASS_STABLE on the negative control I had to write myself - but demonstrating the mechanism on a fixture purpose-built to exhibit the defect does not establish the hypothesis about packs. That is NOT_YET, not PASS, and not FAIL.
disposition_reason: REJECTED as an unqualified PASS. The mechanism is real and I confirmed it works in both directions, and I supplied the negative control the producer omitted, so there is genuine salvageable work here. What cannot be accepted is a PASS on a hypothesis about pack qualification from a unit that qualifies no pack and whose harness cannot be aimed at a real qualifier. The remedy is concrete and uses material already committed in the same cohort: wire the harness to unit 017's qualify_pack, comparing an in-process call against a subprocess invocation on the same pinned pack. Recommend re-verdict to NOT_YET pending that, plus a structured fail-closed path for non-conforming targets and adoption of the stable-qualifier negative control.
followups_for_coordinator: The harness has no real-world reach: it requires a bespoke prime_producer_memory()/qualify() interface implemented by nothing except its own fixture. Reviewer-observed: pointing it at unit 017's qualify_pack.py yields 'AttributeError: module 'synthetic_qualifier' has no attribute 'prime_producer_memory''. Wire it to unit 017's engine over the pinned pack to make the claim real.

The harness does not fail closed on a non-conforming target - it raises an unhandled AttributeError instead of returning a structured error and a non-zero code, which is inconsistent with the fail-closed behaviour every other unit in this cohort implements.

Adopt the negative control I wrote: a stable qualifier with no process memory must yield PASS_STABLE. Reviewer-verified that it does, but the producer shipped no such test, so nothing in the committed suite would have caught a harness that always reports divergence.
